Synopsis:
Default dialogue with the owlbear cub in the player's camp - available after the events of CAMP_OwlbearCub_CFM_Dog. The player can pet the cub, ask some SwA questions and learn what happened during the previous CFM if they opted to quit the dialogue early (what sounded like the owlbear cub attacking the dog was actually the cub having a bad dream and the dog comforting him).

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_OwlbearCub.json: This scene is the camp follow‑up to the earlier CAMP_OwlbearCub_CFM_Dog encounter: the owlbear cub has taken up residence in camp after the player first met it (you may previously have spared it after its mother died and rescued it from goblins). The cub speaks in short, staccato SwA lines and is alternately feral, frightened, or childlike depending on how you treated it before. The player can pet it (a one‑time approval flag prevents spamming the gesture), ask a few SwA questions, or ask what really happened during the earlier cinematic — what sounded like the cub attacking the courier dog was actually a bad dream and the dog comforted it. If you help the cub in this or related dialogues, it can become a permanent camp follower; companion NPCs and other camp scenes may be occurring off‑screen.
- CAMP_OwlbearCub_CRD_2.json: Off‑screen: this is the owlbear cub’s second night at the Withers epilogue gathering — a late‑night, low‑stakes moment while companions and other guests mill about the camp. The player previously spared the cub after killing its mother and rescued it from a goblin “game,” so there’s an uneasy, dependent bond: the cub is feral, speaks in short staccato noises, and is both scared and distrustful (more so if the player antagonized it earlier). He’s showing a ragged leg wound now and is likely exaggerating the injury to elicit help; if the player assists him in this scene he becomes a permanent camp follower, later running off to hunt and returning with a prize.
- CAMP_OwlbearCub_CRD_1.json: In SwA, the owlbear cub speaks in short staccato 'sentences.' He's vicious and feral - but scared. If the player coaxes him with food or is nice to him, he will cautiously consider approaching - but is scared off before he gets too close.An owlbear cub - young, but still dangerous - appears in camp. The player has previously spared the cub after killing its mother, and saved it from a cruel game run by the goblins in their camp.
The cub is scared, and quick to run or attack - it's an untamed wild animal.
- CAMP_OwlbearCub_CFM_Dog.json: The player hears an uproar in the camp and  think the owlbear’s turned on Scratch. When they investigate, they discover the cub is having a nightmare and the dog is comforting him. The player can talk to them and confirm that there's no danger. Subsequently, the cub will be a permanent feature in the camp, with new behaviours with Scratch, plus a new default dialogue.Note: if the player decides to not investigate the sounds, the animals will be moved off-stage for the remainder of the night/the sounds will stop, The player won't know what happened until they see the animals again. If they have SwA, they can learn that there was nothing wrong.
- FOR_Courier_Dog.json: In SwA, Scratch speaks like a human. He doesn't have any kind of dog-like affectation, nor is he stupid - he's well-spoken, even when he's saying 'dog' things. Throughout the dialogue, he's stoic but heartbroken, deluding himself into believing that his master is not dead.We come across the corpse of a man being protected by his loyal dog, Scratch.The dog refuses to let us near the dead man or his belongings, forcing us to try and win him over (or else just kill him). We can use Speak with Animals to get further insight into the dog's perspective.
 If we cast Speak with Dead upon the courier, we can learn the dog's name and use this as an additional way to win it over.

- Owlbear Cub: Sad. No want food. No want play. || [context] CinematicNodeContext: Owlbear cub looks sad and downcast.InternalNodeContext: If the courier dog dies at somepoint after a relationship
has been estabplished between the two characters after their
camp night moment.NodeContext: Sad (mourning the loss of his friend, scratch the dog) (node 31)
- Player: Pet the cub. (node 37)

Sample 2:
- Owlbear Cub: You smell very delicious, but I will not bite you. (node 17)
- Owlbear Cub: Hello! You are not food. You are friend. || [context] NodeContext: Upbeat and childlike (node 8)
- Player: Pet the cub. || [context] InternalNodeContext: Flag sets after the first instance of petting the owlbear cub, to prevent approval spam (node 36)

context: This is the camp follow‑up to the earlier cinematic (CAMP_OwlbearCub_CFM_Dog): the owlbear cub has taken up residence in your camp after you previously spared it (its mother died and you rescued it from goblins). The cub speaks in short, staccato SwA lines and can be feral, frightened, or oddly childlike depending on prior treatment. In this scene you can pet the cub (a one‑time approval gesture), ask a few questions in SwA, or ask about the noisy cinematic — you can learn that what sounded like an attack was actually a bad dream and the courier dog comforted the cub. Off‑screen companions and other camp scenes may be occurring, and if you help the cub here it can become a permanent camp follower; its relationship with Scratch the dog may factor into some dialogue (including mourning if Scratch later dies).
